topic: Continuous Batching & Chunked Prefill: Eliminating the GPU Bubble in LLM Serving Engines
audience: ML Platform Engineers & High-Throughput Inference Architects
title: Continuous Batching and Chunked Prefill: Maximizing Tensor Core Saturation
lead: Static request batching creates massive GPU compute bubbles while waiting for the slowest token generator to terminate. By transitioning to iteration-level continuous batching and chunked prefill, production inference engines saturate GPU tensor cores and smooth time-to-first-token variance by 4.2x.

stats.title: Inference Fleet Utilization & Latency Variance:
items: Static batching leaves tensor cores idling for up to 65% of execution time due to early-finishing request bubbles.
Chunked prefill bounds single-step prefill size to 512 tokens, eliminating decode starvation and reducing P99 latency spikes by 76%.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: The Rotating Airport Baggage Carousel vs. A Tour Bus
mentalModel.text:
In a tour bus, all 40 passengers must wait on board until the final passenger boards before the vehicle departs; when one passenger leaves, everyone else sits stalled.

Continuous batching is a baggage carousel: Pieces of luggage (tokens) smoothly drop onto the conveyor belt and leave the carousel the exact moment they finish, keeping the belt moving at maximum linear capacity 100% of the time.

graph TD

    Scheduler --> Slices["Split Long Prefill into Fixed 512-Token Chunks"]

codeContent:
class IterationLevelScheduler:
    def __init__(self, max_batch_tokens: int = 2048, chunk_size: int = 512):
        self.max_batch_tokens = max_batch_tokens
        self.chunk_size = chunk_size
        self.prefill_queue = []
        self.decode_pool = []

    def schedule_next_iteration(self):
        current_batch = []
        allocated_tokens = 0
        
        # 1. Prioritize active decodes (1 token per active sequence)
        for req in self.decode_pool:
            current_batch.append((req, 1, "decode"))
            allocated_tokens += 1
            
        # 2. Fill remaining budget with chunked prefill slices
        budget_left = self.max_batch_tokens - allocated_tokens
        for req in list(self.prefill_queue):
            if budget_left <= 0:
                break
            tokens_to_take = min(req.remaining_prefill, self.chunk_size, budget_left)
            current_batch.append((req, tokens_to_take, "prefill_chunk"))
            req.remaining_prefill -= tokens_to_take
            budget_left -= tokens_to_take
            if req.remaining_prefill == 0:
                self.prefill_queue.remove(req)
                self.decode_pool.append(req)
                
        return current_batch

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Static batching is unviable for production LLM serving due to variable generation length disparities.
Chunked prefill prevents long 32k prompt ingestion from blocking real-time token generation for existing users.
Combining iteration scheduling with paged virtual memory enables 3x higher serving density on identical hardware.
takeaway.badge: Iteration-level execution transforms bursty prompt arrivals into continuous, predictable GPU saturation.

topic: Long-Context KV-Cache Compression: StreamingLLM, SnapKV, and Heavy Hitter Eviction
title: StreamingLLM and Heavy-Hitter Eviction: Infinite Context with Bounded Memory
lead: Deploying conversational agents for multi-day streaming tasks quickly exhausts physical GPU memory. Naively dropping early tokens causes perplexity to explode. By preserving critical initial attention sinks alongside rolling local windows and heavy-hitter tokens, models process millions of tokens in constant memory.

stats.title: Streaming Inference Benchmarks:
items: Retaining just 4 initial attention sink tokens prevents softmax denominator collapse across 4,000,000+ sequential tokens.
Heavy Hitter Oracle (H2O) evicts 80% of intermediate KV positions while preserving over 99.2% accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack evaluations.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: The Architect's Desk Pinboard
mentalModel.text:
An architect does not keep every intermediate draft paper strewn across their working desk. They keep the permanent project charter pinned at the top-left corner (attention sink), the most recent 10 working drawings in front of them (rolling window), and selectively pin 3 critical structural blueprints in the center (heavy hitters).

Attention Sinks stabilize the softmax denominator: Transformers dump unallocated attention probability into the first few tokens. Evicting them ruins attention distributions entirely.

codeContent:
import torch

class StreamingKVCache:
    def __init__(self, n_sinks: int = 4, window_size: int = 512):
        self.n_sinks = n_sinks
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.k_cache = None
        self.v_cache = None

    def update(self, new_k: torch.Tensor, new_v: torch.Tensor):
        if self.k_cache is None:
            self.k_cache, self.v_cache = new_k, new_v
            return self.k_cache, self.v_cache
            
        self.k_cache = torch.cat([self.k_cache, new_k], dim=-2)
        self.v_cache = torch.cat([self.v_cache, new_v], dim=-2)
        
        seq_len = self.k_cache.shape[-2]
        if seq_len > self.n_sinks + self.window_size:
            # Keep initial sinks + recent window, evicting the middle
            sink_k = self.k_cache[:, :, :self.n_sinks, :]
            window_k = self.k_cache[:, :, -self.window_size:, :]
            self.k_cache = torch.cat([sink_k, window_k], dim=-2)
            
            sink_v = self.v_cache[:, :, :self.n_sinks, :]
            window_v = self.v_cache[:, :, -self.window_size:, :]
            self.v_cache = torch.cat([sink_v, window_v], dim=-2)
            
        return self.k_cache, self.v_cache

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Softmax requires tokens to absorb residual attention mass; the first 4 tokens act as universal sinks.
Pure sliding window attention fails because removing the initial tokens induces catastrophic perplexity surges.
Combining attention sinks with selective eviction allows infinite streaming conversations with bounded constant RAM.
takeaway.badge: Attention sinks turn memory-bounded LLM streaming from a hardware impossibility into a solved problem.

topic: FP8 and Microscaling Formats (MXFP4): Sub-8-Bit Matrix Multiplications on Modern Hardware
audience: Deep Learning Systems Engineers & Hardware Performance Specialists
title: FP8 and Microscaling Formats: Unlocking 2x Compute Density on Modern GPUs
lead: Scaling large language models beyond 100 billion parameters strains memory bandwidth and arithmetic units. Moving from FP16 to FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) and Open Compute Project Microscaling Formats (MXFP4) doubles tensor core throughput while mitigating catastrophic activation outliers.

stats.title: Hardware Throughput & Memory Compression Ratios:
items: FP8 tensor core operations achieve 2x raw TFLOPS throughput compared to 16-bit half precision on NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell architectures.
MXFP4 scales small blocks of 32 elements with an independent 8-bit scale factor, preserving numerical dynamic range with 75% memory savings.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: A Multi-Gear Bicycle vs. A Fixed Single-Speed Hub
mentalModel.text:
A fixed single-speed bicycle forces a rider into a single gear ratio; when encountering a steep mountain, the pedals stall, and on a steep descent, the legs spin uselessly.

Microscaling provides a dynamic micro-gearbox for every 32 numbers: Rather than forcing an entire multi-gigabyte weight matrix into a single fixed range where outliers crush precision, every block of 32 weights gets its own private scale exponent.

codeContent:
import torch

def mxfp4_block_quantize(x: torch.Tensor, block_size: int = 32):
    # Reshape input tensor into micro-blocks of 32 elements
    orig_shape = x.shape
    blocks = x.view(-1, block_size)
    
    # Calculate shared 8-bit scale per block (power-of-two exponent)
    max_abs = blocks.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp(min=1e-12)
    shared_exp = torch.floor(torch.log2(max_abs))
    shared_scale = 2.0 ** shared_exp
    
    # Normalize blocks by shared exponent
    normalized = blocks / shared_scale
    
    # Quantize to 4-bit representation (e.g. E2M1: 1 sign, 2 exp, 1 mantissa)
    q_blocks = torch.clamp(torch.round(normalized * 6.0), -6.0, 6.0) / 6.0
    dequantized = (q_blocks * shared_scale).view(orig_shape)
    return dequantized, shared_scale

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: E4M3 format is optimal for forward passes and activations due to higher precision; E5M2 is optimal for gradients due to wide dynamic range.
Per-tensor quantization fails in deep networks because activation outliers in residual streams crush small values to zero.
Microscaling formats standardize 32-element tiling directly into silicon, eliminating software quantization dequantization overhead.
takeaway.badge: Hardware microscaling unlocks sub-byte tensor arithmetic without sacrificing representational accuracy.

topic: GraphRAG: Knowledge Graphs and Hierarchical Leiden Community Summarization
audience: Knowledge Systems Architects & Enterprise AI Leads
title: GraphRAG and Hierarchical Community Summarization: Conquering Global Dataset Synthesis
lead: Standard vector similarity retrieval fails when asked global thematic questions across thousands of documents. By extracting entity-relationship graphs and clustering them via the Leiden algorithm into hierarchical communities, GraphRAG enables comprehensive cross-corpus synthesis.

stats.title: Global Query Synthesis Benchmarks:
items: GraphRAG demonstrates an 82% improvement in answer comprehensiveness on global dataset summarization compared to baseline RAG.
Hierarchical community summaries reduce token consumption during multi-hop reasoning by over 68%.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: Street View vs. Satellite Multi-Spectral Imaging
mentalModel.text:
Vector search is like zooming into street-level photography of individual storefronts; it finds specific addresses quickly but cannot answer what the city's overall zoning architecture looks like.

GraphRAG provides hierarchical satellite orthomosaics: Raw text is parsed into entity nodes and relation edges, then clustered into county, city, and neighborhood summaries.

Leiden community clustering partitions large entity graphs without manual taxonomy curation.
Map-reduce hierarchical querying produces predictable token utilization across millions of records.
